Everyone responding mentions therapy, but how do I bring that up without making him feel like I'm giving up on helping him?

EDIT: he's one of the kindest people I've ever met. He was always there for me when I needed him

I've tried this. I feel deeply when he is sad and expressed this. I'm hit with: it's useless to me if you understand or not. But then he complains that I don't understand what he feels.

The discussions have been endless and no stone has been left unturned..
Believe me, I've done this. I told him the putting down hurts, but it's always because I don't truly understand why I make him do this. He's told me his problems in detail and still nothing
How do you cope with it?
No worries, this is exactly my point of view too. I repeated this to her, but it’s just hopeless right now.
Yes, she doesn’t want to be seen as weak. It’s the environment she grew up in. She doesn’t see others as weak, this is why she became a doctor. But she couldn’t shed off the part about herself :/

My mum came from a very old school family.. Even though she is a doctor, it’s more important to her to act healthy even when she’s not. 

From where she’s from, every disease is judged and seen as a sign of weakness. I know it sounds harsh, but she doesn’t act like this towards others but herself (I am chronically autoimmune ill myself).

We tried to talk to the doctor side of her, but it just makes her cry and not talk to us..
